title: The Parthenon's architectural illusions are a myth | New Scientist
description: Optical illusions thought to have influenced the design of the Parthenon in ancient Greece are not backed up by evidence or are too small to have an effect
author: Chris Simms

title: We may finally have a way to rate a quantum computer’s usefulness | New Scientist
description: Determining how useful different quantum computers are has been a long running challenge – now researchers appear to have the answer
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Roman roads weren't so straight after all | New Scientist
description: Detailed data on the Roman Empire’s entire road network is offering fresh insight into how Romans built their infrastructure and how it influenced the future geography of Europe
author: James Urquhart

title: LSD could be approved for anxiety in the US in 2027 | New Scientist
description: The psychedelic drug LSD eased anxiety in a late-stage trial, paving the way for a probable approval in the US within the next two years
author: Carissa Wong

title: One of the fundamental forces is stronger than we thought | New Scientist
description: The most precise calculation yet of the electroweak force could help fix cracks in the standard model of particle physics
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Reading for pleasure boosts memory, empathy and mental health | New Scientist
description: Fewer people are reading for pleasure, but getting lost in a good book has repeatedly been linked to substantial cognitive benefits
author: Clarissa Brincat
